---
title: "The History of Major League Baseball"
---

Major League Baseball’s home-run story looks different when seasons of different lengths are compared by rate. The **Home runs** page charts home runs per team-game across history, showing that even the shortened seasons fall within the broader range of seasonal rates.

The career leaders are headed by Barry Bonds with 762 home runs, followed by Hank Aaron and Babe Ruth. The **Sluggers** page ranks the top 15, highlights careers overlapping 1994-2009, and looks more closely at Bonds' season-by-season totals. Explore both analysis pages from the navbar.
